headline: Nvidia Slides 5.86% as Chip Rout Deepens and Huang's Return Stays Under Scrutiny
body_html:
NVIDIA fell 5.86% on Tuesday, moving more market value than any other company as the AI chip selloff resumed. The stock was hit as the board's decision to bring Jensen Huang back as chief executive kept attention on the company's directors. The US Attorney General offered public praise for the company, but questions about the reinstatement lingered over the shares.

The damage spread across the sector. Semiconductors averaged a drop of 7.63%. Micron fell 11.01% after a downgrade, AMD lost 8.86%, Broadcom slipped 3.98% on a report about a Google chip order, and TSMC eased 3.83%. The S&P 500 finished down 0.51%, while the Nasdaq, heavy with the affected names, dropped 1.99%.

Beneath the surface, money rotated rather than fled. Of 662 stocks tracked, 372 rose and 288 fell. Healthcare gained an average 2.57%, Consumer Discretionary added 1.90% and Consumer Staples rose 0.85%, while Financials lost 1.57% and Industrials gave up 1.03%. The session showed a market punishing one crowded trade while leaving the rest of the tape mostly intact.

briefs.headline: Micron Takes the Hardest Hit Among Chip Giants
briefs.body: Micron sank 11.01%, the steepest drop among the largest chip names. A downgrade added to the pressure as the AI selloff resumed. The decline followed a sharp swing in the stock the session before, leaving holders of chip funds to absorb the whipsaw.

briefs.headline: Broadcom and TSMC Slip on AI Worries
briefs.body: Broadcom fell 3.98% as a report about a Google chip order clouded the outlook for AI spending. TSMC lost 3.83% in sympathy. Apple was a rare large-cap bright spot, rising 1.43% while its chip-sector peers sold off.

briefs.headline: Smaller Chip Names Suffer the Deepest Cuts
briefs.body: Ambarella dropped 19.96%, Semtech 16.97%, MaxLinear 16.74% and Ichor 16.49%. Connectivity names Astera Labs and Credo Technology fell 13.88% and 13.07%. Shrinking AI margins at HPE, which overshadowed an upbeat forecast, added to the unease.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Leads the Rotation
briefs.body: Healthcare was the best sector, averaging a gain of 2.57%. MiniMed rose 14.09%, Legend Biotech 11.90%, Mirum Pharmaceuticals 11.19% and Sanofi 10.97%. Roche's expectation that a newly approved cancer pill could become its top seller added to the sector's tone.

briefs.headline: Retail Turnaround Stocks Take Off
briefs.body: Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 19.80% and Dick's Sporting Goods gained 14.60%. Consumer Discretionary rose an average 1.90%. The moves fit a growing view that retail turnarounds are taking hold just ahead of the holiday shopping season.

briefs.headline: Tariff Plans Loom Over a Soft Industrial Tape
briefs.body: Industrials lost an average 1.03% and Financials fell 1.57%. Sources say the administration is set to unveil new tariffs following a probe into excess factory capacity. Traders will watch Wednesday, November 25, for any detail on the measures.
